# Disagreement Log — Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 60

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Agents:** EMET (literal) | LOGOS (formal) | PNEUMA (dynamic)
**Total Disagreements:** 10

---

## Disagreement 1 — 60:1 "additional work" vs. "work he did beyond the commandment"

- **EMET:** "the additional work he did beyond the commandment"
- **LOGOS:** "the work he did beyond the commandment"
- **PNEUMA:** "that extra work represents what he chose to do beyond what was strictly required"
- **Greek:** *to perisson tēs ergasias* — the surplus/extra of the work
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "the additional work he did beyond the commandment" (EMET). "Additional" captures *perisson* (surplus/extra) better than LOGOS's omission of the term; PNEUMA adds "strictly required" not in the text.

---

## Disagreement 2 — 60:2 "not content to give the commandments alone" vs. "not content merely to give the commandments"

- **EMET:** "was not content to give the commandments alone"
- **LOGOS:** "was not content merely to give the commandments"
- **PNEUMA:** "wasn't content just to give the people commandments"
- **Note:** Minor variation.
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "was not content merely to give the commandments to the people" (LOGOS). "Merely" is more idiomatic; EMET's "alone" is also correct.

---

## Disagreement 3 — 60:2 "bore their sins" — all agree

- **EMET:** "he himself bore their sins"
- **LOGOS:** "he himself bore their sins"
- **PNEUMA:** "he also carried their sins himself"
- **Note:** All three agree on substance.
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "he himself bore their sins." The emphatic "himself" (*autos*) is important — the Son personally assumes the burden.

---

## Disagreement 4 — 60:3 "not being at all defiled" vs. "not being defiled in any way"

- **EMET:** "not being at all defiled while conducting itself"
- **LOGOS:** "not being defiled in any way in its conduct"
- **PNEUMA:** "completely free from defilement throughout its time"
- **Note:** Minor variation.
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "not being defiled in any way in its conduct upon the earth" (LOGOS). "In any way" is the standard negation of *oudamōs*; PNEUMA's "completely free" over-translates.

---

## Disagreement 5 — 60:4 "flesh which had served the spirit blamelessly" — all agree substantially

- **EMET:** "this flesh, which had served the spirit blamelessly"
- **LOGOS:** "this flesh, which had served the Spirit blamelessly"
- **PNEUMA:** "this flesh — which had served the Spirit without any fault"
- **Note:** Agreement on substance.
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "this flesh — which had served the Spirit blamelessly." "Blamelessly" (*amemptōs*) is the standard term.

---

## Disagreement 6 — 60:4 "found pure and without spot" vs. "found pure and unspotted"

- **EMET:** "found pure and without spot"
- **LOGOS:** "found pure and unspotted"
- **PNEUMA:** "found pure and spotless"
- **Greek:** *hagnē kai aspilos* — pure and unspotted/spotless
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "found pure and unspotted" (LOGOS). "Unspotted" preserves the negative form *aspilos* more precisely than "spotless" (which is positive).

---

## Disagreement 7 — 60:5 "fragile and imperishable" (EMET error) vs. "fragile and perishable"

- **EMET:** "the flesh is fragile and imperishable" (apparent error — should be "perishable")
- **LOGOS:** "the flesh is fragile and perishable"
- **PNEUMA:** "isn't flesh fragile and mortal?"
- **Greek:** *hē sarx asthenes kai phthortē* — the flesh is weak and perishable/corruptible
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "the flesh is fragile and perishable" (LOGOS). EMET has an error — "imperishable" is the opposite of the Greek *phthortē* (perishable/corruptible). This is noted as a translation error.

---

## Disagreement 8 — 60:5 "this corruptible" vs. "this perishable nature"

- **EMET:** "this corruptible does not put on incorruption"
- **LOGOS:** "this perishable nature cannot put on incorruption"
- **PNEUMA:** "this mortal nature cannot be clothed with immortality"
- **Greek:** *to phthārton hoti ou dynastai endysasthai tēn aphtharsian* — the perishable cannot put on incorruption (cf. 1 Cor 15:53)
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "this perishable nature cannot put on incorruption" (LOGOS). The deliberate echo of 1 Cor 15:53 is preserved; PNEUMA's "mortal/immortality" pair is the 1 Cor 15:54 vocabulary rather than 15:53.

---

## Disagreement 9 — 60:5 "unless first the holy spirit is joined to it" vs. "unless first the Holy Spirit is joined to it"

- **EMET:** "unless first the holy spirit is joined to it"
- **LOGOS:** "unless first the Holy Spirit is joined to it"
- **PNEUMA:** "unless the Holy Spirit first joins it"
- **Note:** Capitalization and word order only.
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "unless first the Holy Spirit is joined to it" (LOGOS). The divine title is capitalized; "is joined to it" preserves the passive — the Spirit's joining is not self-initiated.

---

## Disagreement 10 — 60:5 "subservient to the spirit" vs. "made subservient to the Spirit"

- **EMET:** "the flesh will be subservient to the spirit"
- **LOGOS:** "the flesh will be made subservient to the Spirit"
- **PNEUMA:** "the flesh will become subject to the Spirit"
- **Greek:** *hupotaktirai tō pneumati* — will be subordinated/made subject to the Spirit
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "the flesh will be made subservient to the Spirit" (LOGOS). The passive "be made subservient" reflects the divine action; "become subject" (PNEUMA) implies the flesh's own agency.

---

*End of disagreement log for Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 60.*
